sections.content:
In general every math students can do MATH4999 instead of the 499x based on your track, in case you successfully find a supervisor for your project you want to do. In my case, the professor wanted to have some introduction for the concept of renormalization group, so he assigned me to read a book he recommended, and do something with it. I guess this is a general thing a professor will do when a professor wants to learn something new since I've heard similar cases (outside HKUST).

However, the appointed textbook is written in a way that no physical intuition is involved. Although I'm a math student, I still feel painful because of the nature that the concept of renormalization group came from physics - In a layman way, it aims to resolve the issue of divergence and infinitude coming from calculations identified to be "unphysical".

Therefore, I choose to find other suitable materials based on the topic. Eventually, renormalization group becomes one of the small topics I covered for my project, and I precisely covered the following topics (May not in order):

===I. Statistical and quantum theory===

1. Thermodynamics (Laws of thermodynamics, as background)
2. Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics formulated by differential geometry (Rigorously introduce the concept of phase space)
3. Classical statistical mechanics (In particular, introduce the canonical ensemble and explain how the quantity like exp(-k_B T) arises
4. Ising model and Landau theory (The only place including renormalization group)
5. Quantum statistical mechanics (Density matrix becomes a key physical quantity)
6. Path integral in quantum mechanics, deduction of Brownian motion in physics and Feynman-Kac formula

===II. Mathematical topics===
7. General representation theory of K-algebras (Take half of MATH5112 as reference; Serves as algebric background material)
8. C* and von Neumann algebras (Important backgrounds of quantum mechanics and algebraic quantum field theory).
9. Existence and nonexistence of density matrix in different quantum theories, using type classification of von Neumann algebras
10. Differential Geometry (Background of everything in classical mechanics and classical statistical mechanics)
11. A brief introduction to algebraic quantum field theory. It takes LITERALLY every mathematical concepts I introduced above to continue, and if I can do so, there is something I can write for renormalization group in AQFT. Unfortunately it seems I can't :(
sections.teaching: I basically did everything by myself. As I mentioned, the professor himself didn't know much about the topic of renormalization group, although I didn't do something majorly on this.
sections.grading: The grading for capstone project/fyp courses is generally good and more lenient than regular courses.
sections.workload:
I collected multiple reading materials for several months, and then LaTeX-type my material for 1 month. It turns out that 1 month is not quite enough for me, and actually there is a large room for me to elaborate given that I already finished over 130 pages.

Do collect materials and start early, and try not to let the semester you will do your capstone project filling with too many courses, then I guess the journey will eventually be enjoyable!

sections.content:
In MATH 4999, you can self-designed the project title and everything in the report. Personally, I am particularly interested in the financial market so I did something related to financial statistics (Volatility Modeling, Sentiment, Time-series study, stochastic modeling, etc) quantitative trading (options pricing, derivatives trading, and arbitrage trading), and trading using machine learning with different strategies (CNN, RNN, GAN, SVM, etc). As a student in both math and CS, basically, I just want to explore everything I learned and apply them to real-world scenarios.

In the project, I also explored different programming languages like Python, R, STATA, MATLAB, C#, and the most important one --- LATEX, which is a useful and common immediate to write mathematics reports. I think it could be a fruitful research experience for both your postgraduate and career development.

LATEX: https://www.overleaf.com
sections.teaching:
There is no teaching and guideline in this course. Everything in the report is self-learned. However, if you face some difficulties, I think you could ask the supervisor. Although I only contacted my supervisor 3 to 4 times in the whole semester through email, I believe they are more than happy to answer your questions. Just to be reminded that work under a supervisor that is capable to teach you. However, if you are interested in pure mathematics, you can find professors that have strong research interests in algebra or geometry. If you are interested in applied Mathematics, you can find a professor that has a strong interest in physics, engineering or biological mathematics, etc.

https://www.math.hkust.edu.hk/people/faculty.php
sections.grading:
The only grader of this course "seems" to be your supervisor. From most of the students I know who also enrolled in MATH 4999, most of them can get at least B+/A-. However, I think it really depends on the effort you spent, and the supervisor's preference.

I am not sure if the grading scheme is different among supervisors, but for most of the supervisors, the only grading component is your report.

Grade: A
sections.workload:
Light. Personally, I just spent around 15 days completing the project, with around 5 hours per day. 12 days for the project content and 3 days for writing a report using LATEX. 75 hours should be light for a 3-credit course, especially when you love what you are doing. But it really depends on your effort and the difficulty of your report.

Also, I know some of the students contacted the supervisor in advance and completed half of the work in the summer. So you can have much better time management in the fall semester.
